Pakistan · Fuel Prices

Fuel cut again: petrol down to Rs335, diesel to Rs364

Prices at the pump fall again for Thursday 12 November 2026: petrol is down Rs3 to Rs335 per litre and high-speed diesel is down Rs7 to Rs364 per litre under OGRA's daily review mechanism — the seventh straight day of cuts. The government's tax take is unchanged, at Rs114 per litre on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Top Stories

10 policemen martyred in Kohat ambush; 18 attackers killed

Ten policemen were martyred and 12 injured when a police team returning from a joint operation against illegal gold mining in Kohat's Darbukach area was ambushed on Wednesday. KP Police say 18 attackers were killed in the hours-long gun battle, and the TTP later claimed responsibility.

Dawn·Pakistan

PM Shehbaz seeks $188bn for clean energy at COP31

Speaking at Wednesday's high-level clean-energy session at COP31 in Antalya, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said Pakistan needs about $138bn for low-carbon power generation by 2035 plus $50bn to swap coal for solar, and pressed partners for concessional finance and affordable technology. Clean energy is now nearly 55% of Pakistan's energy mix, he said, with some 22,000MW of rooftop solar added in two years.

Express Tribune·Pakistan

ADB approves $500m disaster financing for Pakistan

The Asian Development Bank has approved $500 million in contingent disaster financing for Pakistan under its policy-based lending, so budget support can flow quickly after eligible disasters such as floods and earthquakes. The package forms part of the second subprogramme of the bank's Climate and Disaster Resilience Enhancement Programme.

Dawn·Pakistan · Economy

Lahore stays world's most polluted city as smog grips Punjab

Lahore remained the world's most polluted major city on Thursday, with its air quality index at 346 in the morning after touching 444 at the same time a day earlier, while several other Punjab cities — including Raiwind, Bahawalpur and Multan — recorded AQI levels above 500.

Kohat attack & minerals forum · Thursday 12 Nov 2026
Pakistan · Kohat Attack

Kohat ambush: 10 policemen martyred, 18 militants killed

A police contingent returning from a joint operation against illegal gold mining in the Darbukach area of Kohat district was ambushed on Wednesday, and the exchange of fire ran for hours. Ten officers were martyred — among them DSP Gambat Haider Zaman and Sub-Inspector Mukhtiar — and 12 others were injured, while KP Police say 18 attackers were killed; the banned TTP later claimed responsibility for the attack.

Pakistan · Investment

Pakistan showcases mineral wealth as two-day investment forum opens in Islamabad

The two-day Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 opened in Islamabad on Thursday, with Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar urging international investors and mining companies from more than 60 countries to explore the country's mineral sector. Provincial leaders used the forum to pitch their own opportunities — from Punjab's pink salt and iron ore to Balochistan's Reko Diq copper-gold project — as the government promised a predictable, investor-friendly environment.

World · Ukraine War

US envoys arrive in Moscow for Putin talks as capitals trade strikes

US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow on Thursday to brief President Vladimir Putin on two days of US-mediated Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, where negotiators agreed a large prisoner exchange but remained divided over territory. The diplomacy unfolded as Russia and Ukraine exchanged fresh strikes on each other's capitals overnight.

World · Gaza

Israeli strike on Gaza's Nasser Hospital kills six, including a surgeon

An Israeli airstrike hit a building at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, early on Thursday, killing at least six people — among them surgeon Rezik Abushira — and wounding 20 others, according to Palestinian health and civil defence officials. The strike hit the hospital's surgery department and caused extensive damage inside the complex.

Cricket · Thursday 12 Nov 2026
Sports · Cricket

Debutant Saqib Khan takes seven as Sri Lanka fold for 446 in Rawalpindi

Sri Lanka resumed day four of the Rawalpindi Test at 404 for 4 but lost their last six wickets for just 42 runs, bowled out for 446. Dhananjaya de Silva made 167 and Kusal Mendis 119, while debutant pacer Saqib Khan finished with seven wickets as Sri Lanka took only a 12-run first-innings lead over Pakistan's 434 for 9 declared; Pakistan were 39 for 1 at lunch.
